waveSpec.structure: L-8 — structure over gates, wherever the class allows it. (1) Deleting `InstanceType<typeof X>` from demo/palettes makes the layer inversion UNREPRESENTABLE: with no instance handle there is no cross-layer write, no latent cycle, and no `?.` swallow to reason about — the cure is a deletion of expressive power, not a rule. (2) The AdminGate at the composition boundary makes `getAdminToken()` a non-null contract inside the console, so all 22 `if (!token) return` early returns delete: the unauthorized state stops being a state the panel must model because the panel never mounts unauthorized. (3) Hoisting the disclosure into AdminListItem gives 'an admin list row' exactly one home, so the skeleton is honest by construction rather than by comment. Where structure is genuinely unavailable I say so and gate instead: the dead-`variant` class cannot be made unrepresentable from demo/ — glass-ui's Button accepts it via $attrs fallthrough and vue-tsc types it as an HTML attribute (proven: exit 0 over 51 live instances) — so the demo side gets a grep gate plus a DOM assertion, and the structural half (inheritAttrs:false + an explicit allowlist so an unrecognised design-token prop is a visible no-op) leaves as a BH-relay letter. Per the masking-fallback ban, no local shim, wrapper or lint plugin may stand in for the producer's change.

result.dissent: Three places where I part company with the challenger fleet, and one place where I part company with the registry. (1) The BLOCKER is misplaced. L-1 was crowned on four uniqueness claims and a reproduction, and I could refute all five: the '25 = 24 barrels + useAdminUsers.ts:14' arithmetic never held (the grep does not match line 14 at all), useSlugMigration.ts is the same inversion in the same directory, ColorPicker.vue exposes 12 members to AdminUsersPanel's 5, and the data-loss scenario is unreachable because a template ref is null exactly when the instance holding the state is gone — I read vue 3.5.35 runtime-core.cjs.js:2846-2860 to close the one path (KeepAlive deactivate) that could have saved it, and deactivate moves the subtree without touching the ref. The real BLOCKER on this file is L-5: an unauthenticated stranger is told as fact that the roster is empty, on a route with no auth meta, and handed operable destructive controls. I verified it live with a discriminator the seat never built — hasUnreachable=false and skeletons=0 prove no request was attempted, so the empty plate is the token-guard branch and not an artefact of this API-less dev server. That distinction is the whole difference between a finding and a false positive here, and I want it on the record because the brief warned me about exactly this trap and the trap was avoidable by construction. (2) Counts were repeatedly asserted where they had not been scoped: 35 barrel importers measured 48; '11 files inject SAFE_ACCENT_KEY' measured 6; AdminListItem.vue:13 is :11, AdminListSkeleton.vue:12 is :9, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:99 is :98, AdminPane.vue:133 is a comment. Every direction held and no row died of it — but a fleet that gets four line numbers and three counts wrong in eleven rows is not yet at L-9 discipline, and rows that live on counts must carry the right ones. Conversely I reproduced 51/22, 22/11, 24, 11, 22 and 17 to the unit, so the fleet is not unreliable — it is unaudited, which is what this seat is for. (3) The whole evidentiary base is uncommitted. `git ls-files docs/tranches/V/megatranche/ | grep -c png` = 0; .gitignore:34 swallows every capture both seats cite, including the 'certified' safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png that L-5 leans on and all ten frames A..J. Under L-7 those witnesses do not exist, and both reports read as though they do. Every finding I confirmed, I confirmed from code or from my own re-run — none of it rests on a screenshot I cannot fetch from a git object. (4) Against the registry: the CHALLENGE-D seat's 18 rows against this same file are on disk and in no harvest JSON and no ledger row. The formation's own L-13 says work that was paid for is harvested before anything is re-deployed; 18 rows against the largest component in the palettes area are currently outside the registry, and if this component is declared adjudicated on the strength of my eleven verdicts, four accusations carrying BLOCKER severity vanish without a verdict. I have named them in CARRIES rather than adjudicating them, because adjudicating an unharvested report would launder it into the record by the same route.

verdicts.rescopedTo: The specimen line is neither legible-as-truth nor round-trippable, in two disjoint ways: (a) five CSS-native rows print coordinates outside the destination space's gamut with no mark, and the BROWSER silently clamps them on paint — `hsl(346.045357898758deg -1295.152156124318% 103.662622110611% / 82.7%)` computes to rgba(255,255,255,0.827), pure WHITE, three centimetres from a swatch painting lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827); (b) four rows (hsv, kelvin, ictcp, jzazbz) emit a `space · a · b · c` pseudo-syntax that neither the browser nor value.js's own parseCssColor accepts. The cure is a per-row GAMUT MARK plus a distinct non-CSS presentation form — explicitly NOT gamut projection.
verdicts.note: I set out to confirm this and refuted its stated mechanism instead. The challenger's headline is `Out-of-gamut, NON-CSS-PARSEABLE channel values ship to screen … would not parse`. Both halves of the parse claim are false. Browser test (chromium, `el.style.color = caption` against an rgb(1,2,3) sentinel): rgb(385.3…) ACCEPTED → rgba(255,143,200,0.827); hsl(… -1295% 103.66%) ACCEPTED → rgba(255,255,255,0.827); hwb(… -51.1%) ACCEPTED → rgba(255,143,169,0.827); color(display-p3 1.402…) ACCEPTED; color(srgb-linear 2.580…) ACCEPTED. CSS Color 4 defines out-of-range component values and clamps or gamut-maps at use time — they are valid by spec. Library test against the shipped dist: `parseCssColor` returns ok:true for all five, and `convertColor(parsed,'lab')` returns lab(92.000000000000, 88.800000000008, 20.000000000005 / 0.827) for RGB, HSL, HWB and Display P3 alike — i.e. the un-projected specimens round-trip LOSSLESSLY back to the original color. That is decisive against the proposed cure: folding `mapColorToGamut` into the formatter, as L-3 asks, would replace an exact statement with a lie (it would print rgb(255 143 200) for a color that is demonstrably not that color) and would destroy the one property that makes the row worth printing. The cure is REFUTED and must not be built. What survives, and is worth a gate, is what I measured rather than inherited: the browser CLAMPS these strings on paint, so the number the user reads and the color any downstream tool would produce diverge (the HSL row reads as a pink and paints as white); and the four non-CSS rows use a hand-rolled `·`-separated grammar that parseCssColor returns ok:false on, which is the genuine "will not parse" arm — and it is not the arm the challenger named. The two unused helpers cited (picker-color.ts:195 clampPickerColor, :119 mapPickerOklabToSrgb) are real and unused on this path, but their absence here is correct, not defective.

The three cited code regions all exist and the inference from them does not. MixConfigBar.vue:99-118 and GradientVisualizer.vue:181-194 are near-identical inline Select blocks — I read both — but they iterate INTERPOLATION_SPACES from color-space-meta.ts:26, a NINE-member list of {value,label,description} triples whose semantic is 'spaces you may interpolate a gradient or mix THROUGH', explicitly authored at S.W5-6/F16 as its own vocabulary. ColorSpaceSelector iterates DISPLAY_COLOR_SPACE_NAMES, an EIGHTEEN-member map whose semantic is 'spaces the picker may express the current color IN' and which necessarily includes non-interpolable members (hex is an encoding, kelvin is a one-channel scalar, ictcp/jzazbz are HDR appearance spaces). These are two different concepts that share a noun. Collapsing them into one component — the proposed cure — would either offer hex and kelvin as gradient interpolation spaces or amputate the picker catalog to nine; it is precisely the shared-wrapper contrivance the KISS edict bans. The narrowing-idiom contrast also cuts the other way: the workbench blocks narrow with `(v: AcceptableValue) => v as PickerSpace`, a typed cast, while this component uses `(colorSpace: any)` — so the two 'duplicates' are the BETTER-typed instances, and the defect is L-12's, already booked. What is genuinely repeated is markup, not domain: four-plus `Select > SelectTrigger > SelectItem v-for` blocks over `{value,label,description}` lists (both space selects AND both hue-method selects, HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS being the fourth), which is a list-driven-Select shape the producer could ship. Relayed as a glass-ui observation; refuted as a color-space ownership defect.

waveSpec.structure: Structure, not gates, per L-8 — three defect classes are made unrepresentable and only the residue is gated. (1) `satisfies Record<DisplayColorSpace, SpaceEntry>` makes 'a space with no info row' a compile error: adding a SpaceId to picker-color.ts fails tsc until its info and its doc DECISION exist, so ColorNutritionLabel's `: colorSpaceInfo.rgb` and ConsoleRail's `as any` have nothing left to mask and delete rather than being forbidden. (2) `defineModel<DisplayColorSpace>({ required: true })` plus a key-preserving catalog array makes the four `any`/cast holes unspellable at the boundary — a host cannot write `(colorSpace: any)` because there is no emit to write it on, and `space as DisplayColorSpace` disappears because the array never erased the key. (3) One `formatSpecimen` returning a discriminated `{ form: 'css' | 'channels' }` makes 'two grammars in one 12-line function' unrepresentable: the caller cannot emit a CSS-shaped string for a non-CSS space because the form is data, not a branch. Gates are retained only for the properties a type cannot carry — pixel legibility, live gamut marking, dot uniqueness, and the About-pane truth check — because those are rendering facts, not typing facts.

result.addendumClause: ADDENDUM CLAUSE (proposed for FORMATION-LAWS, as an addendum to L-9 — not a patch of it, per EDICT E-3). **L-9.1 — a "sole offender" is a claim about a scope, and the scope is part of the claim.** Evidence: four of the fifteen accusations against ColorSpaceSelector booked a repo-wide condition as a component defect because the grep that found it was scoped to the component's own directory. `grep -rn '"\.\./ui/' demo/color-session/` returns 1 and yielded "Sole offender"; the same grep at `demo` returns 90 statements across 48 files in 7 trees (L-4). `tag="div"` reads as this component's surviving legacy; a multiline scan of all 23 `<WatercolorDot>` elements shows 21 carry it (L-8). `inject(SAFE_ACCENT_KEY)!` reads as this component's deviation; it is the house contract at 6 consumers (L-5). The tsconfig↔exports drift reads as this component's dependency chain; it is a program-wide config row with no component locus and no live break (L-14). Law: any accusation containing the words *sole*, *only*, *unique to*, or *the one place* must paste the SAME command re-run at repository scope beside the scoped one, and must book the row at the scope where the count lives. **Corollary — a wave inherits the scope, not the accusation.** A repo-wide condition placed behind a component-sized gate produces a wave that cannot close on its own evidence, which is the L-1 failure ("an arc wearing a wave's name") arriving through the back door of a mis-scoped grep. **Second corollary — the cure is adjudicated separately from the defect.** L-3 stated a true fact (out-of-gamut coordinates ship to screen) and attached a cure that would have made the product worse: re-derivation shows the un-projected specimens round-trip losslessly through `parseCssColor` → `convertColor(·,'lab')` back to lab(92, 88.8, 20 / 0.827), so the proposed `mapColorToGamut` fold would have replaced an exact statement with a clamped lie — and would have been landed under a GREEN gate, because nobody had written the gate that says the numbers must still round-trip. A challenger's `proposedCure` inherits no evidential weight from the evidence establishing its `defect`, and every wave that adopts one must state the property the cure could break and gate it in the direction that would catch it.
result.dissent: I dissent from the challenger fleet on five rows and from its own severity ordering on one, and I record two errors of my own. **Against the fleet.** (1) L-3 is the significant one: its stated mechanism ("non-CSS-parseable … would not parse") is false in both witnesses I could reach — chromium accepts all five out-of-gamut specimen strings via `element.style.color`, and value.js's own shipped `parseCssColor` returns ok:true for every one, with `convertColor(·,'lab')` recovering lab(92, 88.8, 20 / 0.827) to within 1e-11. waveSpec.structure: STRUCTURE, not gates, does five of the eight cures — formation law L-8. (1) The ink duplication dies by DELETING the dual path: after the rewrite `useSafeAccentFn('resting')` is the ONLY way this component can obtain a certified accent, so the hand-assembly is not discouraged but absent — and MT-MD-12's probe-epoch omission becomes unrepresentable, because the composable no longer folds the referent at all and useSafeAccentFn calls bumpProbeEpochOnMount at useContrastSafeColor.ts:348. The docstring at useContrastSafeColor.ts:363-368 naming `useMarkdownColors` as the beneficiary of `resolveSurfaceLightnessLive` is deleted in the same commit, so the widening loses its written justification and can be retired by the sibling wave that owns HeroBlob.vue:99. (2) The silent-undefined lookup dies by deleting the fourth hand-copy of the union: `Partial<Record<DisplayColorSpace, DocModule>>` makes 'space with no guide' a TYPED value the compiler forces the caller to handle, instead of a cast-laundered undefined. The `as` is what made the wrong thing expressible, and the `as` is gone. (3) The exception channel dies at the type level: the composable's return becomes `ComputedRef<Record<string,string>>` with `{}` as the total degenerate — there is no error path left to convert. (4) The content inversion dies by MOVING the files: once the guides live at demo/scenes/about/content/, there is no path from assets/ into demo/ that could be inverted, and assets/ ceases to exist. (5) The seam's `any` dies by typing. TWO cures genuinely need a gate, and I state why each is unavoidable rather than assert it. (a) The Skeleton prop API: the wrong thing is expressible because glass-ui's prop surface is the module boundary — we cannot make a foreign component's props unrepresentable from inside the demo — so a scoped strictTemplates program is the only instrument available. (b) CSS/corpus correspondence: a stylesheet cannot be typechecked against markup, so the only structural option is a golden that re-derives the rendered tag set from the corpus itself and compares it to the styled set — bidirectional, so it fails equally on a dead rule and on a rendered element left unstyled.

### ADD-MDG · The document module

**MDG-1 · Content lives in the scene that renders it.** No file outside `demo/` may name a path inside `demo/`. A reference document, a fixture, a snippet — if the app is its only consumer, it lives in the app's tree and imports downward. Enforced by `grep -rn 'demo/' assets/` = 0 and, after this wave, by `assets/` not existing.

**MDG-2 · A theme may only style markup its own corpus emits.** Where a component renders a CLOSED corpus, the styled selector set and the rendered selector set are equal, and the equality is re-derived from the corpus by a command — never asserted by a comment. Speculative CSS is not harmless surface: 146 of 331 lines here were adjudicated by two prior rulings (AB-3, and the F6 ONE-grammar law) against markup that has never rendered, which means those rulings entered the audit record as evidence about nothing. Dead CSS does not merely sit there; it manufactures findings.

**MDG-3 · One concept, one composable — and a widened surface is a confession.** A consumer that cannot see an existing composable rebuilds it, and the library is then widened to legitimise the rebuild. When an export's docstring names its beneficiary by name (`resolveSurfaceLightnessLive` naming `useMarkdownColors`), that sentence is the defect's own signed statement: the response is to fix the call site and delete the widening, never to keep both. **Corollary, earned here:** when a helper's docstring states an obligation on its consumers (`bumpProbeEpochOnMount`), a consumer that takes the helper and skips the obligation is defective even when the omission does not currently fire — the contract was written from a measured failure (3.59:1) and the next consumer will not be so lucky.

**MDG-4 · The Result contract is not re-openable at the render boundary.** A `computed` may not `throw`. The library is failure-explicit by charter; a consumer that answers `!ok` with an exception re-introduces, inside the render path, the exact channel the library exists to eliminate. Decoration has a degenerate — return it. This binds even where the throw is presently unreachable: an unreachable throw is a latent one.

**MDG-5 · A cast is not a type.** `x as NarrowUnion` at a `Record` lookup converts what would be a compile error into a silent render omission. Where a map is partial, say `Partial<Record<Canonical, T>>` and handle `undefined`; where it is total, make the compiler prove it. The fourth hand-copy of a union is not a fourth opinion — it is three unnoticed drifts.

**MDG-6 · A surface with no URL has no audit.** Every route-driven gate — the visual sweep, e2e, the perf sweep — is structurally blind to a pane-only surface. Until such a surface is addressable, its π obligation is discharged by an explicitly stated non-route capture, and any report claiming `blankOrNearBlank: 0` over a route matrix states, in the same breath, which surfaces that matrix could not see.

**MDG-7 · A prop the producer does not declare is a lie, not a hint.** Passing `surface`/`variant` to a component whose props are `{ class }` reads as intent and ships as an inert HTML attribute. Where the producer's API cannot express the design intent, that is a producer change under the glass boundary — relayed, never locally overridden, never masked with a fallback.

**MDG-8 · A closed-corpus claim is measured over the corpus, not over one document.** A DOM census of the currently selected item generalised to eleven is the MT-F006 shape wearing new clothes. Where the corpus is enumerable, render it and take the union.

SIX DISSENTS AND ONE CONCURRENCE-WITH-CAVEAT, each byte-grounded.

**(1) AGAINST L-1's PRIORITY CLAIM — the one the root asked me to judge on its merits, and it does not survive.** The row says "Land FIRST: this is the only defect that makes the rest of the repo's evidence untrustworthy." I tried to confirm it and could not. Local `dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` and the installed `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` export the **same 52 symbols** — I extracted and diffed both export lists and the difference is empty. The entire 382-vs-350 divergence is private type-name forks (`Alpha_2`, `Channel_2`, `ChannelsBySpace_2`, `Color_2`, `SpaceId_2`, and `[S in CssColorSpace]: Color_2<S>` where the tarball has `Color<S>`), and TypeScript is structural: those are mutually assignable. `npm run typecheck` exits 0. `/value` has zero demo importers. So exactly zero pieces of existing repo evidence are invalidated today, and the strongest TRUE statement is the narrower one the challenger also made: `pretypecheck: npm run build` rebuilds dist for every typecheck, and `/css` — 10 sites, 9 files — escapes that rebuild by falling through to a frozen 4.0.0 tarball. That is a real, cheap, prophylactic fix that should land before V·π reshapes `src/css/`. It earns priority on **cost and sequencing**, not on epistemic contamination. Overstating it is not free: a formation that has manufactured seven false findings in one session cannot afford a BLOCKER whose headline its own measurement refutes.

**(2) AGAINST L-2's CURE, ON A MEASURED NUMBER.** "Both verifiable by `eslint --print-config` and one vue-tsc run; neither needs a design decision." I built the program and ran it: **271 errors**, 263 TS2353 + 8 TS2322, across demo/palettes 134, demo/workbenches 65, demo/shell 44, demo/scenes 14, demo/shared 4, demo/color-session 4, demo/color-picker 4, demo/picker 2. Many are `aria-label` and `data-*` on glass-ui components — an attrs-fallthrough question at the producer boundary, which is exactly a design decision. Three of the 271 are this component's. A cure that opens 271 errors in one wave is the "arc wearing a wave's name" that formation law L-1 forbids, and had it been adopted as written it would have failed on contact.

**(3) AGAINST L-7's LIVE-DOM SUB-MEASUREMENT, which is the very error the formation laws were written from.** The row records `a: 0` from a Playwright census of `.markdown-wrapper .markdown-body`. Over the corpus, `a` IS rendered — three anchors, at `lch.md:13`, `oklch.md:13`, `xyz.md:13`. The probe read the ONE document for the then-selected space and the row generalised to eleven. That is MT-F006's shape exactly (60 captures of the same screen reported as a route matrix) and L-9's law verbatim. I replaced the instrument: render all eleven documents through the repo's own markdown-it and take the union — `a code em h2 h3 hr li ol p strong ul`. The row survives intact, indeed strengthened (21 dead selector groups, mechanically re-derivable), but the method must not be copied. I also correct the count: the stated ranges sum to 149, not 142, of which 3 lines must survive for the one live `> h2 + h3` pair — **146**.

**(4) AGAINST L-10's CURE.** `Record<DisplayColorSpace, GuideModule>` requires seven newly authored reference documents. That is a content obligation, not a type change, and a wave carrying it cannot close. `Partial<Record<DisplayColorSpace, DocModule>>` plus deleting the `as` gets the whole structural benefit — the lookup types as `DocModule | undefined`, the `v-if` becomes a total handler instead of an accident, and no future space can be laundered — while leaving the seven missing guides as one honestly banked row owned by the wave that measured them. result.addendumClause: ADD-CSP-F (worker-F) — the configurator population, four clauses. (1) PAINTED-EXTENT OBLIGATION: every bounded numeric control renders its value as a painted extent at ≥3:1 against its own track; a token-presence argument (the T.W8 :202 pattern — 'the track ink is certified') can never close a value-legibility row, because contrast of an information-free surface is not information (PROPORTION-AUDIT law 8 applied to controls). (2) RESET-DOMAIN HONESTY: a reset affordance may write ONLY the keys its surface declares; whole-object restore (Object.assign AND useConfiguratorState.resetCurrent alike — the semantics, not the API, is the defect) is forbidden wherever any sibling system holds live state under the same root. (3) COMMENT-PARITY IS GATED: a CSS block whose stated cure a measurement refutes (the inert clamp, the zero-adding ::before, the phantom fade mask, the ≥44px claim) is deleted WITH its comment in the same cut — a lying comment is a doc-truth defect of the same rank as the dead code it defends, because it is what the next reader builds on. (4) THE COARSE RUNG IS THE PRODUCER'S: glass-ui ships @media(pointer:coarse){[data-control-target]{min-block-size:var(--touch-target,2.75rem)}} (dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css:1) on every control root — consumers may not re-mint per-instance hit-area extensions; a wanted rung beyond 44px is a relay, never a ::before.

Adopt the producer machine for clone-guard/isDirty/per-row canReset only. (2) D-2's BLOCKER 'unreachable' framing is factually wrong: this seat measured one tap (dock Blob toggle) mounting all 31 rows at 390x844. The composition defect is real, but it is the canon-forbidden global-toggle amputation pattern — band-owned (M-13/MT-F028) — and the severity argument should rest on the toggle's illegality, not on false unreachability. (3) C-8/D-5's WCAG 2.5.8 framing over-claims: the operable target of this producer slider is the full track (precedent measurement on the identical component; tracks here 432-962x24), and the effective coarse rung is the producer's [data-control-target] rule this seat located — the pane's blocks are inert scaffolding, and the surviving demo defect is purely the false comment. STATIC: SFC:92-94 `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` replaces whole top-level keys; importing BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS from dist/blob-config.js prints `color.paletteStops: ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]` — the canned triad IS on defaults, so `config.color` is replaced wholesale; BlobPane.vue:8-9 declares that key OUT of the slider domain ('the live picker-palette feed … not a slider'); useAtmosphere.ts:389-403 writes it from `watch(atmosphereColor, …)`, keyed on the colour string, so it will not re-fire until a DIFFERENT colour is picked. The asymmetry is structural, not incidental: aurora-atoms.ts `DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS` carries NO `seed`, so the same code preserves the aurora seed at depth 1 and destroys the blob palette at depth 2 — reset semantics decided by nesting depth. LIVE (my own probe, gate G1): before ["#ffbde0","#ffdde5","#fff6f6","#fff6f4"] → after ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]. The wave's strongest row; BUILT as gate G1.

verdicts.id: C-2 — all config sliders ship an empty aria-valuetext
verdicts.rescopedTo: 34 sliders carry NO aria-valuetext, so unit-bearing and formatted domains announce a bare unformatted number and the in-repo one-voice formatter sits unconsumed — but the 'screen readers announce a 17-digit float' framing is refuted
verdicts.note: The absence is CONFIRMED by my own DOM read: 31/31 rows on /#/blob have `aria-valuetext === null` while the row renders `0.220` (gate G2). The same-page picker population carries real text — `"Lightness 92.0%"`, `"a axis 88.8"`, `"Alpha 82.7%"` — from demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/composables/useSliderAnnouncements.ts (U.W-A11Y · U-F27), so the asymmetry and the unconsumed cure are real. I REFUTE the harm framing: `0.2199999988079071` is a CDP AXValue float32 artifact, not an assistive-technology fact — the shipped attribute is `aria-valuenow="0.22"`, and ARIA announces valuenow when valuetext is absent. The surviving harm is precise: `Hue Range` (degrees) and `Merge (ms)` announce a bare integer with no unit, `Body Radius` announces 0.22 against a rendered 0.220, and a second formatter would drift — hence G2 asserts EQUALITY with the rendered readout, not merely non-emptiness. The producer forwards only aria-label/labelledby/describedby (slider-DzqeQmMu.js:134-137, re-read), so the clean prop-through is BANK B-3.

verdicts.id: C-3 — variant="spectrum" is a dead prop; the pane's own --slider-track-bg defeats it
verdicts.rescopedTo: the missing value read is CONFIRMED and is GLASS-OWNED; the prescribed cure ('retire the variant so the producer's .slider-range paints') is REFUTED by measurement and may not be gated in a demo-only wave
verdicts.note: Defect CONFIRMED with tighter numbers than the accusation: on /#/blob the range is laid out to the value EXACTLY — 163.47/432 = 0.37840 against a declared (0.22−0.08)/(0.45−0.08) = 0.378378 — and paints `rgba(0,0,0,0)` with `background-image: none`; on /#/atmosphere 731.13/962 = 0.7600 for Colour Energy 0.76. Producer CSS confirms the mechanism is by recipe: `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{ -webkit-backdrop-filter:none; box-shadow:none; background:0 0 }`. CURE REFUTED by three experiments of my own: (a) flipping `data-variant` to the real default `"standard"` (Slider.vue props `variant:{default:"standard"}`) yields rangeBg `oklab(0 0 0 / 0)` — STILL transparent — and a `.slider-thumb` of width 0, because the thumb's width/opacity rule is `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb` only; (b) `.glass-slider:not([data-variant=spectrum]) .slider-range` painting rules in dist/glass-ui.css = 0; (c) even an injected consumer rule `.config-console .slider-range{background:oklch(0.55 0.19 25)!important}` computes transparent, and feeding the documented `--slider-range-bg` moves `--liquid-fill-tint` while `background-color` does not move. The fill is NOT reachable from the demo at glass-ui 7.0.0 at any specificity — BANK B-1 + BH relay, not a gate. Entanglement no other seat recorded: demo/styles/foundation.css:571-574 is the OWNER-RULED, banked restatement of glass's own spectrum-range rule (the dist drops the unprefixed `backdrop-filter:none`); its selector is keyed to `[data-variant="spectrum"]`, so retiring the variant SILENTLY ORPHANS a live bank.

verdicts.id: C-4 — copyAsJson() awaits writeClipboard and discards its Result
verdicts.note: Re-derived live, both documented failure modes forced on the real button in my own probe. `navigator.clipboard = undefined` → bodyTextChanged false, aria-live regions in the pane 0, button.disabled false, aria-disabled null. `writeText` rejecting NotAllowedError → bodyTextChanged false, and the only trace is the producer's console warn `[useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected: NotAllowedError: Denied`. Success is equally silent. C-4's producer reading is the one the two challenger seats disagree about, and it is correct: `writeClipboard` returns a Result and never throws (see the D-10 verdict). The LAN arm is real and re-checked: vite.config.ts sets `server.host: true` and `navigator.clipboard` is secure-context-gated, so Copy JSON is a dead button on the exact origin that setting exists to serve.

verdicts.id: C-5 — unguarded dot-path read: `as number` + fmt().toFixed unmounts the pane mid-render
verdicts.rescopedTo: a type-level lie that is LATENT through today's shipped UI but LIVE as an authoring hazard, because SliderDef.key is an unchecked `string` on the AuroraPane side
verdicts.note: The type does permit the state: `AuroraAtoms.zones?: AuroraZones` is optional (atoms.d.ts:145) and AuroraPane.vue:103 declares `{key:"zones.count"}`, while AuroraPane guards the SAME key three lines away (`atoms.zones?.count ?? 4`, :82). My node re-run of the boundary table reproduces the challenger's exactly: 0→"0", −0→"0", 0.5→"0.500", NaN→"NaN", Infinity→"Infinity", 1e21→"1e+21", undefined→TypeError, null→TypeError; the catcher is demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:59 `onErrorCaptured` returning false, which is why nothing reaches pageerror. I did NOT re-run the injection (probe parsimony; the challenger labelled it INJECTED itself) so the unmount arm stays a HYPOTHESIS. What I add, and what makes it live rather than curious: BlobPane's 13-line `NumericAtomPath` guards ONLY BlobPane's key literals — `SliderDef.key` is plain `string`, so a one-character typo in AuroraPane's SECTIONS compiles and crashes the pane at first render. Cured structurally by G8's typed lens (L-8), not by a runtime guard.

verdicts.id: C-6 — 31 orphan <label> elements and zero programmatic grouping
verdicts.note: My own census: /#/blob labelCount 31, labelsWithFor 0, labelsWrappingControl 0, groupOrHeading inside `.config-console` 0, and all 7 `.config-section-title` elements are `{tag:"SPAN", role:null}`; identical on /#/atmosphere at 3/1. Producer confirmation re-read from ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts, whose own header states 'No a11y for/id wiring' — the gap is the producer's by design and the consumer never supplied the missing half. The `for` route genuinely cannot work (reka's thumb is `span[role=slider]`, not a labelable element), so the durable fix is `aria-labelledby`, which the Slider forwards but ConfiguratorRow does not expose (BANK B-3). The section-group half needs nothing from anyone: `role="group" :aria-labelledby` on the wrapper the pane already draws (SFC:123-127). Gate G3.

verdicts.id: C-7 — the clamp and the coarse-pointer ::before are both provably inert
verdicts.note: Both arms re-measured by me. CLAMP: container 512px → `min-block-size` resolves 35.84px, rendered row 60.97px; container 1042px → clamp ceiling 42px, rendered row 60.97px — across a 2.04× container range the rendered rhythm moved 0.00px, under a comment declaring 'THE ONE RHYTHM SOURCE' (SFC:208-217). distinctRowHeights = [61] on both desktop arms. ::BEFORE: on a 390×844 coarse-pointer context the producer's `.glass-slider` root already measures 44px tall, so `block-size: max(100%, var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem))` resolves max(44px,44px) = 44px and adds exactly zero; I confirmed `--dock-touch-target` = `2.75rem` and the pseudo-element's computed block-size = 44px against a host of 44px. Gate G5a. The wave's cleanest deletion: two heavily-commented blocks whose comments assert cures the measurements refute.

verdicts.id: C-8 — 12px thumbs under a '≥44px touch rung' comment
verdicts.rescopedTo: the geometry is CONFIRMED (12×24 pointer:fine, 12×44 coarse) and the comment at SFC:187 is FALSE — but WCAG 2.5.8 is NOT violated, because the spacing exception is satisfied
verdicts.note: Geometry re-measured: every one of the 31 config thumbs on /#/blob is 12×24, all 3 on /#/atmosphere are 12×24 desktop and 12×44 mobile. SFC:186-187 claims '≥44px slider rows — the producer's own --dock-touch-target'; the rendered ROW is 60.97px but the OPERABLE target is the 12px-wide thumb, so the claim is false as written. I REFUTE the SC framing that both challengers and JUROR-3 assert: WCAG 2.5.8's undersized-target exception applies when a 24px circle centred on the target does not intersect another target's circle — measured row pitch is 67px with exactly one target per row, so 2.5.8 (AA) is MET. Booking a false SC violation is precisely the class of error L-9 exists to prevent, and three separate seats made it. The wave keeps two honestly-named gates: G5c (the false claim leaves the source) and G5b (the 24px inline floor as the HOUSE floor under PROPORTION-AUDIT law 7, explicitly not an SC claim). The glyph itself is producer geometry — BANK B-2, no per-instance override (edict 5).

verdicts.id: C-9 — copy/reset/clone hand-rolled where useConfiguratorState<T> is one import away
verdicts.rescopedTo: the hand-roll and the missing structuredClone guard are CONFIRMED; the prescribed 'adopt useConfiguratorState<T>' cure is REFUTED as specified, because that API is preset-shaped and does not express reset-to-defaults
verdicts.note: The hand-roll is real: SFC:6-10 cites the producer composable as the principle it follows and SFC:88-94 rebuilds it, with no try/catch around structuredClone (the producer's has one), no isDirty, and ConfiguratorRow's `canReset` + `reset` emit unused (both verified present in ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts). The challenger's DataCloneError reproduction re-runs correctly for me. But I read the producer's signature before believing the cure (L-9): `useConfiguratorState<T extends object>(options)` REQUIRES `presets: readonly ConfiguratorPreset<T>[]`, its `resetCurrent()` restores the ACTIVE PRESET's baseline, and its cloneMode is preset-oriented — adopting it does not give 'reset to these defaults', it changes the pane's model to a preset model. The C10 A4 [P1] ADOPT book (N/audit/lanes/C10.md:92-105,265) survives as a BOOK, re-scoped. The wave's cure is smaller and cannot lie about its domain: reset exactly the `SliderDef.key` paths the pane owns (gate G1).

verdicts.id: C-10 — VACUOUS GATE: no test exercises any behaviour of the component
verdicts.rescopedTo: zero behavioural coverage is CONFIRMED and all four green-keeping mutations survive; the 'delete the file and every gate reads green' claim is REFUTED; and the one existing oracle is ADVERSE to the correct cure
verdicts.note: Re-run from scratch: `grep -rln … test/ demo/test/ e2e/` returns exactly two files, both e2e; 19 vitest files under test/ and 3 under demo/test/ mention it zero times (gate G9). I read both oracles rather than trusting a summary. o7-card-census.spec.ts:38-42 EXCLUDES the component by name and substitutes a grep. o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:924-966 asserts only `row.ratio` for `.config-console .configurator-row label` and `.font-mono`; :1161-1210 only `.slider-track`. So M1 (`update()`→no-op), M2, M3 and M4 all stay green — CONFIRMED. But the strong claim is FALSE: o18 awaits `.config-console .configurator-row` visibility, so deleting the file turns it RED. Independently I reached the sharper reading: o18's track leg was born RED against the pre-cure `--secondary` track and green against the `--ink-muted` re-ink, so it certifies the loudness of the INERT surface and will go RED the day the re-ink is retired — a lock, not a vacuum. Sequencing consequence: the oracle is re-aimed in the same cut as any track change, and until B-1 fires SFC:202 may NOT be deleted.

verdicts.id: C-11 — dead v-if branches, a false JSDoc, and child-mutates-parent-prop
verdicts.note: Read directly from the SFC, no probe needed. :44 promises 'Pass empty array to show empty state'; :119 and :163 guard on `sections.length > 0`; there is no `v-else` anywhere, so `sections: []` renders PaneHeader + slot and silently loses Copy JSON and Reset too. Neither consumer passes [] (AuroraPane 1 section, BlobPane 7), so both guards are permanently true. The prop mutation is real: `update()` → `writePath(config, …)` writes into a prop object, against the house idiom stated at aurora-atoms.ts:11 ('the demo's standing injection-key-over-prop-drill idiom') — and both consumers already own the injected object, so the prop-drill is pure loss. Gate G11 for the doc-truth half; the injection-key half rides G8.

verdicts.rescopedTo: real but sub-threshold; FOLDed into G8's typed lens with no gate of its own
verdicts.note: I did not re-run the latency arm — probe parsimony, and the challenger reported it against itself with a number precisely so a later seat could not inflate it (43µs/row; +1.21ms mean for 10× the rows; mutationFanout confirms Vue patches exactly one row per keystroke). verdicts.id: C-13 — the pane does not mount at 390 on /#/blob, so the coarse-pointer block is unreachable there
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as measurement, but already carried by the layout-gestalt band — cross-cited to V·L2, not re-booked here
verdicts.note: My own breakpoint sweep on /#/blob: `.config-console` present with 31 rows at 1440/1280/1100/1024, ABSENT with 0 rows at 1000/900/768/600/390, body text 750→68 chars at the boundary. Mechanism is the shell's (demo/shell/viewSchema.ts maps blob to the right region and the narrow layout does not mount it) — the M-13/MT-F028 anti-pattern. `registry/adjudicated/layout-gestalt.md` WAVE V·L2 already reads 'ConfigSliderPane D-2 → FOLD (DOM half; composition half V·L4)'. Per my brief and per L-5's anti-rename rule I cross-cite rather than author a competing layout cure. The only local consequence is recorded: it is a second, independent reason to delete the coarse-pointer block under C-7 — inert where it applies, unreachable where it would matter.

verdicts.id: D-1 — forced-colors: single-channel track and a vanished focus indicator
verdicts.rescopedTo: split in two — the FOCUS arm is CONFIRMED, DEMO-OWNED and individually curable (gate G4); the TRACK/RANGE arm is GLASS-OWNED (bank B-1). The stated cause (SFC:202) and the stated evidence ('zero forced-colors hits') are both REFUTED
verdicts.note: The row my re-derivation changes most. Measured in Chromium with `forcedColors:"active"` and a `matchMedia` false-witness guard asserted FIRST: focused config thumb `:focus-visible` true, `outline-style: "none"`, `box-shadow: "none"` — no focus indicator; track `rgb(255,255,255)` === well `rgb(255,255,255)`, border-width 0px. The SUBSTANCE holds. The CAUSATION does not. The challenger's `grep -rn forced-colors demo/scenes/` → 0 hits is an L-9 scope error: demo/styles/foundation.css:678 ships a full two-tier WHCM policy and :702-720 binds `:where(… [role="slider"] …):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight }`. I proved the rule is ALIVE with a CONTROL in the same run — the action-bar button one DOM level away gets `outline-style: solid, 2px`. It is defeated ONLY on the thumb, by specificity: `:where()` contributes 0, so the demo rule is (0,1,0) while the producer's `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb[data-v-4f4cab01]:focus-visible{ … outline:none }` is (0,4,0). That converts a BLOCKER attributed to glass material into a demo-owned cascade fix that lands today with no producer. Second demo-owned dead declaration found alongside: the tier-1 roster line at :693 puts `forced-color-adjust:none` on `.glass-slider[data-variant="spectrum"] .slider-range`, and I measured it applying to an element whose background is `rgba(0,0,0,0)` — it preserves nothing. Neither challenger nor either prior juror located either fact.

verdicts.id: D-2 — below 1024px the entire Blob configurator leaves the DOM
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as DOM measurement; already FOLDed by the layout-gestalt band (V·L2 DOM half, V·L4 composition half) — cross-cited, no competing cure authored here
verdicts.note: Same sweep as C-13 (one measurement filed twice by two seats). Present/31 rows at ≥1024, absent/0 rows at ≤1000. I decline the 'unreachable' framing, independently of JUROR-3 who reached it too: a Blob affordance exists one tap away, so a wave built on 'unreachable' would make the pane render at 390 and declare victory while leaving the canon-forbidden global pane toggle standing. The correct home is already open and already names this row: `registry/adjudicated/layout-gestalt.md` V·L2 CARRIES 'ConfigSliderPane D-2 → FOLD (DOM half; composition half V·L4)', with gate g1 (per-route rendered text @390 ≥ 0.9× @1440, RED at 7.7%) and DELTA '#/blob 390: sliders 0→31'. This wave adds only the cross-cite and the schema field V·L4 will need (`SliderSection.rank`), so the composition half has something to compose.

verdicts.id: D-3 — no slider indicates its value; the inert track reads as 100% filled
verdicts.note: Defect CONFIRMED independently, with the strongest numbers in the corpus (arithmetic under C-3: the fill element is laid out to the value within 1e-4 and paints zero alpha, in both routes and both schemes). The figure/ground inversion is measurable, not rhetorical: the inert 962×24 track measures 5.82:1 light and 8.30:1 dark against the well — the SAME ratio as the live readout's ink, because SFC:202 and :204-206 feed both from `--ink-muted` — while the painted extent measures 1.00:1. `Body Radius 0.220` and `Satellites 3` therefore render as identical bars. Diagnosed twice historically and cured neither time (N/audit/lanes2/U-CONTROLS.md:54; N/waves/N.W13.md:28 — both files verified to exist per L-6). What I refuse is the cure, not the finding (see C-3). Disposition BANK B-1 with a runnable re-trigger + BH relay, and the wave states plainly that D-3 does NOT close in this cut — honest, whereas gating it demo-side would produce a wave that cannot go green alone (L-1).

verdicts.id: D-4 — a certified TEXT ink used as a ~23,000px² area fill
verdicts.note: Measured by me: track geometry 962×24 = 23,088px² on /#/atmosphere and 432×24 on /#/blob; `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted, …)` resolves to `oklch(0.447121 0.00386159 34.63)` light and `oklch(0.889964 …)` dark; contrast vs the well 5.82:1 / 8.30:1, identical to the readout ink (same token) and within one stop of the row label in dark (9.28:1). The tier argument holds: text ink is specified for glyph mass, not for a continuous surface. BUT this row is LOCKED by the oracle it was born from — o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1161-1210 asserts `.config-console .configurator-row .slider-track` ≥ GRAPHICS_FLOOR and is green ONLY because of this re-ink; deleting SFC:202 today makes it RED, and the producer fallback (`var(--secondary)`, which the SFC's own comment records at ~1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark) is worse. FOLD into B-1's single cut: track material, spectrum retirement, o18 re-aim and the producer's paint land together or not at all.

verdicts.id: D-5 — 12×24 thumbs and a coarse-only hit extension
verdicts.rescopedTo: identical to C-8 — geometry CONFIRMED, coarse-guard inertness CONFIRMED, WCAG 2.5.8 violation REFUTED (spacing exception satisfied at 67px pitch, one target per row)
verdicts.note: Filed twice by two seats; adjudicated once. See C-8 for the SC analysis and C-7 for the coarse-guard measurement. One addition that sharpens D-5's 'desktop is uncovered' claim: the guard is not merely coarse-only, it is inert ON coarse too — the producer root is already 44px there — so the block covers nobody in either pointer register. Gates G5b (house 24px inline floor, honestly named) and G5c (the false ≥44px claim leaves the source). Glyph geometry itself is BANK B-2; edict 5 forbids a per-instance demo override of a producer control.

verdicts.id: D-6 — 8 dividing lines where the inventory says none, scheme-asymmetric
verdicts.rescopedTo: the COUNT is CONFIRMED (8 on /#/blob, 2 on /#/atmosphere); the scheme-asymmetry claim is REFUTED — the rules measure 1.24:1 light and 1.29:1 dark, no 4.7× swing exists
verdicts.note: Count re-measured from computed style: 7 `.config-section-header` border-bottoms + 1 `.config-action-bar` border-top = 8 on /#/blob, 2 on /#/atmosphere (gate G6). The asymmetry is an artifact, and I caught it in MY OWN first pass before reading any prior seat: a 1×1-canvas helper that fills `#000` and then fills the sample returns the colour PRE-MULTIPLIED OVER BLACK for any alpha<1, fabricating a luminance. My first run reported 5.22 light / 1.19 dark — the challenger's 1.08/5.03 inverted, wrong for the identical reason. Re-solving α from two grounds (draw over #000 and over #fff, recover α and the unpremultiplied colour, composite over the actual well) gives section rule 1.24:1 light / 1.29:1 dark and action-bar rule 1.16:1 / 1.18:1 — forbidden AND too weak to do the grouping job they were added for. This is a HARNESS defect with reach beyond this component: any ledger number produced by a fill-black-then-fill helper against an alpha<1 colour is unsound and should be swept. The one arm that gains force: under Chromium forced-colors these same rules compute `rgb(0,0,0)` and are the ONLY surviving element in the pane.

verdicts.id: D-7 — closed type matrix breached in three roles; heading == row label
verdicts.note: Six-property identity re-measured on /#/atmosphere: `.config-section-title` and `.aurora-row-label` agree on fontFamily "Fira Code", fontSize 16.4px, fontWeight 400, textTransform uppercase, letterSpacing 1.64px, color rgb(112,89,66) — 6/6 — and I confirmed by direct read that the two CSS blocks are byte-identical in all five declarations in the same order (SFC:237-243 vs AuroraPane.vue:194-200). The size-step failure is independent and equally measurable: section heading 16.4px vs row label 16.4px (no step at all), value 11px — the mono voice is louder as a heading than as the data it groups. Gates G10a (computed) and G10b (source, so the byte-copy cannot return). A pure demo-side cure needing nothing from the producer.

verdicts.rescopedTo: structure CONFIRMED; the demo-owned half is banked (B-4) and the 'compose InstrumentChassis' cure is cross-cited to V·L4 rather than re-authored
verdicts.note: Ancestor walk from `.console-well` on both routes returns exactly `[{DIV, ["glass-resting"]}]`, wells 1, and the well computes background `oklab(0.913295 …)`, `1px` border, `12px` radius — a bounded sub-card inside a glass card. foundation.css:339-354 concedes it: '.console-well … INTERIM demo class — swaps onto the producer `.glass-well` rung when packet P3 ships (BOOKED)'. L-6 check on the cited authority: the accusations cite bare filenames; the binding docs are at docs/tranches/V/OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md, /VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md and /PROPORTION-AUDIT.md — NOT under megatranche/design/ where a literal reading would look. They exist. I decline to author the chassis cure here: it is the same object V·L3/V·L4 own, and authoring a second one is exactly the re-booking L-5 forbids.

verdicts.id: D-9 — the essentials/advanced/compare composition is unrepresentable
verdicts.rescopedTo: the API gap is CONFIRMED and the schema field is BUILT here; the disclosure composition is cross-cited to V·L4
verdicts.note: Re-measured: /#/blob scrollHeight 2611 vs clientHeight 695 = 3.76 screens, scroll-region bottom 799 exactly abutting action-bar top 799; /#/atmosphere does not overflow (575/575), so the amputation is route-specific and the count matters. `SliderSection` is `{title, defs}` and `SliderDef` is `{key,label,min,max,step}` (SFC:27-39) — no rank, collapsed, compare, disabled, unit or format, so no consumer CAN express the binding composition. That is what makes it a design defect rather than a missing feature. The disclosure surface belongs with the layout band, so this wave BUILDS only the schema — `SliderSection.rank: "essential" | "advanced"` inside G8's typed lens — so V·L4 has something to compose and nothing is lost between the two waves.

verdicts.id: D-10 — two actions with zero result state; Reset destructive and unconfirmed
verdicts.rescopedTo: the 'zero result state' arm is CONFIRMED; the 'unhandled promise rejection' arm is REFUTED by measurement
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED half: both buttons carry no aria-label, no disabled state, no aria-disabled; aria-live regions inside the pane and its action region = 0; both clipboard failure modes and the success path are silent (see C-4). REFUTED half, and it settles a real disagreement between the two challenger seats: I installed an `unhandledrejection` listener and forced a `writeText` rejection on the real button — `unhandledRejections: 0`, because glass-ui's `writeClipboard` catches internally and returns `{ok:false, reason}` (the console warn is the producer's own). C-4 states this correctly; D-10's `@click` on an async function is NOT an unhandled-rejection hazard, and the cited `void writeClipboard(...)` idiom at three other call sites is a style convention, not a cure. The surviving obligation — one durable status region owned by the pane, and a confirmed, comparable Reset — is BUILT with G1.

verdicts.id: D-11 — the live readout has no tabular figures and no reserved width
verdicts.note: Re-measured by in-place substitution on the shipped readout (gate G7): `font-variant-numeric: "normal"`, `min-inline-size: "auto"`, narrowest legal "3" = 6.8px, widest legal "-0.0005" = 47.4px — a 40.6px swing on an element whose shipped width is 33.9px. The mechanism is exact and structural: `fmt(v) = Number.isInteger(v) ? String(v) : v.toFixed(3)` derives precision from the VALUE, not the declared step, so every BlobPane range containing an integer flips between 5 chars and 1 mid-drag, and `membrane.noiseFreq` (step 0.1) renders three decimals — two digits of false precision — on 8 of 31 rows. `Merge (ms)` smuggles its unit into the label while `color.hueRange` (degrees) has none, because `SliderDef` has no `unit` field. This is the ONLY value channel the pane can own while B-1 is banked, which is why it is a first-class gate and not a polish item.

verdicts.id: D-12 — the 'ONE RHYTHM SOURCE' clamp is inert and bypasses the producer's size API
verdicts.note: Same measurement as C-7's first arm (0.00px across a 2.04× container range), plus the API half which I verified against the producer rather than asserting: `data-size` is null on every row; glass-ui.css ships `.configurator-row[data-size=sm|md|lg]` bound to `--configurator-row-gap-*` / `--configurator-row-py-*`; and ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts documents a three-rung `size` prop resolving local-prop → `CONFIGURATOR_SIZE_KEY` inject → a baked-in `gap-1.5 py-2` fallback. The demo passes `class="gap-1.5 py-1"` (SFC:142) — duplicating the fallback's gap and overriding its padding with a utility — plus a `:deep()` min-block-size correction. Gate G5a; the honest cure passes `size` and deletes both the clamp and its claim.

verdicts.id: D-13 — the bare slot licenses a second control-row species
verdicts.note: Measured on /#/atmosphere: `.aurora-row` label is Fira Code 400 uppercase rgb(112,89,66) at 16.4px sitting directly on the Card, while `.configurator-row` label is Plus Jakarta Sans 500 normal-case rgb(28,25,23) at 16.4px inside `.console-well` — two families, two weights, two colours, two material tiers, and (per D-7) a byte-copied CSS block. AuroraPane.vue:14-15 documents the slot as existing 'for exactly this extra controls case' while SFC:3 documents an `extraControls?` prop `defineProps` never declares — the API drifted from its own header. Cured by the schema: a section entry accepts an enum/select def alongside slider defs so every control is one ConfiguratorRow in one grid; AuroraPane.vue:118-181 and its whole `<style>` block delete with it. Gate G10b pins the byte-copy's death; the unification rides G8.

verdicts.id: D-14 — the reserved spectral meniscus applied to 34 non-chromatic axes
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as a canon breach; its cure is entangled with BANK B-1 and with the banked foundation.css:571 shim, so it does not close in a demo-only cut
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED by direct read and by DOM: `variant="spectrum"` at SFC:146 applies to all 31 BlobPane defs and all 3 AuroraPane defs, and every `.glass-slider` in `.config-console` carries `data-variant="spectrum"`; the domains driven are Body Radius, Smooth K, Rim Power, Shininess, Merge (ms), Zones — none chromatic. I fully endorse the dissent that 'feed the variant a real gradient' is INADMISSIBLE: manufacturing a chromatic ramp for a geometry axis would devalue the signature form to fix the fill. But retirement is not free either, and I am the only seat to have measured its cost: with the variant gone the thumb's width/opacity rule stops matching (measured 0×20), and demo/styles/foundation.css:571-574 — the owner-ruled, still-banked restatement of glass's own spectrum-range rule, added because the dist drops the unprefixed `backdrop-filter:none` — is keyed to `[data-variant="spectrum"]` and would be silently orphaned. Retirement rides with B-1's single cut; no local patch is proposed and the shim is not touched (glass boundary honoured, masking-fallback ban honoured).

verdicts.id: D-15 — dependent-control state was never designed
verdicts.rescopedTo: the model gap is CONFIRMED; the 'five sliders control nothing at Satellites=0' effect claim is UNVERIFIABLE-HERE (producer shader behaviour)
verdicts.note: CONFIRMED half, measured: `SliderDef` has no `disabled`, no `enabledWhen`, no `dependsOn` (SFC:27-33); the template renders no disabled state; `aria-disabled` is null on every one of the 34 thumbs. BlobPane.vue:59 declares `geometry.satelliteCount` over 0..4 and :60-62/:111-112 declare five satellite-parameter sliders. UNVERIFIED half: whether those five are genuinely inert at count 0 is a claim about glass-ui's metaball shader, which I did not instrument — plausible to the point of near-certainty, but I will not book a producer behaviour I did not measure. The wave gates only the representable half (the schema gains a dependency axis; the row renders the producer's disabled state with a reason), and records the effect claim as the BH relay's evidence request.

verdicts.id: D-16 — the prop contract erases types; consumers rebuild them
verdicts.note: Re-counted by grep, scoped to source (L-9: no node_modules, no dist): `(x as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>` appears exactly 4 times in demo/scenes/ (AuroraPane.vue:111,113; BlobPane.vue:124,126), and `as number` once in the SFC (:77) — gate G8. BlobPane.vue:36-48 is a 13-line recursive mapped type under a 24-line comment about stripping the `-?` modifier at two levels, written solely to restore key safety the pane threw away — and it guards only BlobPane's key LITERALS, because `SliderDef.key` is a bare `string` (see C-5). Making the pane generic over its config (`SliderDef<T>['key']` a keyof-derived dot-path union) deletes all four casts, the mapped type and the reflection layer: a net subtraction of roughly 30 lines, and the L-8 structural answer that needs no gate to stay true afterwards.

verdicts.id: D-17 — pane-scroll-fade promises a mask that does not exist
verdicts.rescopedTo: the doc/name-truth half is BUILT here; the edge affordance itself is cross-cited to V·L4 with the disclosure composition
verdicts.note: Measured: `mask-image: none` and `-webkit-mask-image: none` on `.pane-scroll-fade` in both routes and both schemes. I read the class rather than trusting the citation: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 (unscoped block) sets only `contain: layout style paint` and `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block`, and its own comment explains it exists for the scroll-timeline, not for a fade. So SFC:103-105 ('The scroll region owns the fade mask + overflow') is false, and the class name mis-describes nine consumer panes, not one. The amputation it leaves is real (scrollHeight 2611 / clientHeight 695, hard edge at 799). Correcting the comment and the name is demo-owned and lands here (G11 family); adding the mask belongs with D-9's disclosure so the two are designed together rather than a mask bolted onto a flat 3.76-screen list.

verdicts.id: D-18 — RTL half-mirrors the row and promotes the destructive verb
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as latent — no RTL surface ships today; FOLDed into the schema (declared axis direction + LTR-isolated readout) with no standalone gate
verdicts.note: Re-measured by applying `dir=rtl` post-load: the thumb sits at fraction 0.382 from the visual left in BOTH directions (LTR track 769..1201 vs RTL track 239..671 — identical fraction), so the row's text mirrors while its track does not; the readout computes `direction: rtl` with `unicode-bidi: normal`, i.e. not LTR-isolated; and DOM order is Copy JSON → Reset, so in RTL flex direction — not DOM role — promotes the destructive verb to the leading position. The un-mirrored track is very likely correct per the canon's 'numeric axis sign never mirrors', but correct by accident: `.glass-slider` ships `data-inverted` (which flips `--slider-range-origin`), so the axis direction is expressible and unexpressed. No RTL locale ships, so this earns no born-RED gate; it earns a declared field, which is strictly better than a gate nothing exercises.

verdicts.id: D-19 — a truncating row label with no title/tooltip fallback
verdicts.rescopedTo: the structural facts are CONFIRMED; the consequence did NOT reproduce in my re-derivation and stays a labelled latent state, FOLDed into the schema's label budget
verdicts.note: Structural half CONFIRMED: the producer `truncate` class is present, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `title` null, and the full string survives only in the Slider's `aria-label` (SFC:145). Consequence half NOT reproduced here: substituting a 47-character label in place gave clientWidth 389 == scrollWidth 389, `clipped: false` — the label had room, so my re-derivation neither confirms nor refutes the challenger's 392/413 numbers, which were taken with an unstated substitution string. The challenger labelled this a latent state itself (longest shipped blob label 'Click Impulse', 13 chars) and that label is correct. FOLD: a declared label budget on `SliderDef` beats a `title` attribute and is enforceable at authoring time rather than at render time.

verdicts.id: D-20 — a documented empty state with no branch and a prop that was never declared
verdicts.note: Identical object to C-11's first half, filed by the design seat; adjudicated once and gated once (G11). Read directly: SFC:3 documents `extraControls?`; `defineProps` at :41-52 declares only config/sections/defaults/title/description; SFC:44 promises an empty state; the template has no `v-else` anywhere. G11 is a source gate because the state has no runtime to assert against — which is the point: it is documentation asserting behaviour that does not exist, and the mechanically checkable property is the absence of the false line.

verdicts.id: D-21 — dead positioning residue: `relative` on two elements, `mx-auto` on w-full
verdicts.note: The stated evidence is false and the cure is unverified, so the row does not survive. Stated: 'the pane's own tree contains no absolutely-positioned child'. Measured: 64 absolutely-positioned elements render inside the pane root on /#/blob — 31 `.slider-range`, 31 `.slider-thumb`, 1 `.dock-plate`, 1 `.dock-layer`. The conclusion partly survives the evidence's collapse (`containedByPaneRoot: 0` — every one resolves to a nearer positioned ancestor, so neither `relative` is load-bearing today), but the proposed deletion is unverified: removing the `relative` class from BOTH the outer div and the Card leaves both computing `position: relative`, so some other source supplies it and deleting the utility changes nothing measurable. An INFO row whose evidence is false, whose cure is a measurable no-op, and which cannot be gated is RETIRED with this rationale rather than carried — L-5 requires a disposition, not a gate.

verdicts.id: CSP-X1 (shell-dock L-axis carry naming this file) — the dock-tint reader's querySelector('.glass-dock') is document-order dependent because this pane mints a second dock
verdicts.rescopedTo: CONFIRMED as measurement; the SUBJECT is the shell dock-tint reader, so it is cross-cited to the shell band with this file recorded as co-cause
verdicts.note: Extracted from the ledger row keyed to the shell-dock seat, which names demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:164 as the secondary cause — the kind of row that is keyed only by axis text and would be lost by a subject-name-only sweep. Verified live on /#/blob: `document.querySelectorAll('.glass-dock').length === 2` — the first at y=10 is the shell's, the second at y=810 is this pane's `<GlassDock>` action bar (SFC:164, inside `.config-action-bar`). So `querySelector('.glass-dock')` picks the shell today (`firstIsShell: true`) purely by document order, and the breakage on re-order is a hypothesis, correctly labelled as such by the originating seat. This pane is co-cause, not subject: the cure is the producer publishing `--glass-tint-chrome` / `useDockSurfaceTint()` so the demo reads a token rather than a node. Recorded here so the shell band's fix is not written as if only one dock existed, and so the action-region redesign (D-10) knows it is deleting the second dock.

waveSpec.title: The configurator population tells the truth — reset owns a domain, the console announces, the dead cures go, and a type lens replaces the reflection layer
waveSpec.scope: IN SCOPE (all demo-owned; all closable without any other party): demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue — the reflection layer (:57-86), resetDefaults (:92-94), copyAsJson (:88-90), the section wrapper (:123-130), the two inert CSS blocks (:208-230), the two dividing rules (:232-235, :245-251), the stale header/JSDoc lines (:3, :44, :103-105, :186-187); demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue (NumericAtomPath + two casts die); demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue (two casts + the whole <style> block die with the byte-copied .aurora-row-label); demo/styles/foundation.css — the WHCM focus bind at :702-720 gains the specificity it needs for [role=slider], and the inert tier-1 roster line at :693 is decided; NEW demo/scenes/config-slider-schema.ts (typed lens + SliderDef/SliderSection successor); NEW demo/test/scenes/config-slider.test.ts (the anti-vacuity suite). EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, each with a named home: the value PAINT and the spectrum retirement (BANK B-1 + BH relay — measured demo-unreachable at glass-ui 7.0.0); thumb glyph geometry (BANK B-2); ConfiguratorRow aria-labelledby / Slider aria-valuetext prop-through (BANK B-3); the .console-well P3 producer swap (BANK B-4); the narrow-width mount and the preview/inspector composition (cross-cited to registry/adjudicated/layout-gestalt.md V·L2 and V·L4, which already CARRY 'ConfigSliderPane D-2 → FOLD'); demo/styles/foundation.css:571-574 (the owner-ruled spectrum-range shim — NOT TOUCHED; its coupling to variant="spectrum" is why B-1 owns the retirement); docs/tranches/V/vnext/**; scripts/dev/dev.sh (unowned, never touched).
waveSpec.structure: L-8 — this wave prefers structure to gates wherever it can reach. The reflection layer is DELETED, not guarded: SliderDef becomes generic over the config (`SliderDef<T>` with `key: DotPath<T>`, plus declared `unit`, `precision` derived from `step`, `rank: "essential"|"advanced"`, `enabledWhen?`, and a label budget), which makes five defect classes unrepresentable at once — an untyped dot-path (C-5/D-16), a reset that cannot name its domain (C-1), precision inferred from a value (D-11), a control with no dependency axis (D-15), and a section with no disclosure rank (D-9's schema half). The four `(x as unknown) as Record<string, unknown>` casts and BlobPane's 13-line NumericAtomPath delete as a consequence, not as a chore: roughly 30 lines net subtracted. Only where structure cannot reach does the wave add a gate: computed style (G4, G5a, G6, G7, G10a), rendered ARIA (G2, G3), live behaviour (G1) and source-truth (G5c, G8, G9, G10b, G11). BUILD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: G9 (anti-vacuity) lands FIRST, because the tree's only existing oracle is ADVERSE — o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1161-1210 certifies the loudness of the inert track and goes RED the day that re-ink is retired. A wave that meets a lock mid-flight is tempted to preserve the defect to keep the gate green, which is exactly how the T.W8 cure produced D-3/D-4.

gates.gate: G1 · RESET-DOMAIN — Reset restores only the key paths the pane declares
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY, pasted from the run: `color.paletteStops BEFORE ["#ffbde0","#ffdde5","#fff6f6","#fff6f4"] → AFTER ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]`. The input that makes it RED is one click on Reset at /#/blob while a picker colour is live: `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` is depth-1 and `color` IS on BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS, so the nested live feed inside it is replaced by the canned triad and useAtmosphere.ts:389-403 (keyed on the colour string) will not re-fire. Stays RED for any future whole-object merge; goes green only when reset names the SliderDef key paths it owns.

gates.gate: G2 · ONE VOICE — every config slider announces the value its row renders
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `rows whose aria-valuetext !== rendered readout: 31/31. e.g. {"label":"Body Radius","readout":"0.220","valuetext":null,"valuenow":"0.22"}`. Asserts EQUALITY with the rendered cell, not non-emptiness, so a second formatter drifting from the one the eye reads fails it — the failure the picker population already solved once (useSliderAnnouncements.ts, U-F27). A unit-bearing row (`Merge (ms)`, `Hue Range`) announcing a bare integer also fails it.

gates.gate: G3 · GROUPING — drawn structure is programmatic: a named group per section, zero orphan labels
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `sections drawn 7; named role=group 0 (want 7); orphan <label> 31/31 (want 0)`. Inputs that make it RED: a section rendered as a bare <span> title over an unlabelled wrapper (SFC:128-130), or any <label> with neither `for` nor a wrapped control. `for` cannot work against span[role=slider], so the passing form is role=group + aria-labelledby on the wrapper the pane already draws, with the row name bound via BANK B-3 when the producer ships it.

gates.gate: G4 · FORCED-COLORS FOCUS — the demo's own WHCM focus bind reaches the config thumbs (CHROMIUM ONLY)
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `focused config thumb: focus-visible true, outline-style "none", box-shadow "none" — NO focus indicator. CONTROL in the same register: the action-bar button gets outline-style "solid" 2px.` The control assertion is the gate's teeth: it proves demo/styles/foundation.css:678 + :702-720 EXISTS and WORKS and is defeated ONLY on the thumb, by specificity — `:where(…)` contributes 0, so the demo rule is (0,1,0) while the producer's `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb[data-v-4f4cab01]:focus-visible{outline:none}` is (0,4,0). Re-lowering the demo selector into `:where()`, or moving focus back to box-shadow, makes it RED again. FALSE-WITNESS GUARD (L-12/I-20): the gate asserts `matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)').matches === true` FIRST and FAILS rather than passes when false — WebKit ignores Playwright's forcedColors, so a WebKit forced-colors frame is void evidence, never a green one, and playwright-webkit never stands in for safari-app.

gates.gate: G5a · DEAD CURE (rhythm) — a declared container-scaled rhythm actually moves the rendered row
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `container 512px → min-block-size 35.84px, rendered 60.97px; container 1042px → 42px, rendered 60.97px. Across a 2.04× container range the rendered row moved 0.00px under a comment declaring "THE ONE RHYTHM SOURCE".` Any clamp re-asserted BELOW the row's real content height fails it. It passes either by deleting SFC:215-217 + :142 and passing the producer's `size` rung (ConfiguratorRow's documented three-rung axis; `data-size` is null on every row today), or by a rhythm that genuinely responds — never by a comment.

gates.gate: G5b · HANDLE FLOOR — the operable handle meets the house 24px inline floor on pointer:fine
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `3 handles, distinct sizes ["12x24"] (want inline ≥ 24). Row pitch 67px and one target per row, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception is SATISFIED — this gate is the house floor (PROPORTION-AUDIT law 7), not an SC violation, and the SC claim must not be made.` Deliberately named honestly: booking a 2.5.8 violation here would be a false finding, which three prior seats made. A demo-side ::before re-appearing fails it on principle (edict 5) even if the number passes — the cure is producer seat geometry (BANK B-2), so this gate is reported RED rather than weakened while the bank stands (L-2: a gate that cannot be made RED is deleted; a gate whose cure is elsewhere is banked, never softened).

gates.gate: G5c · DOC TRUTH (touch) — the SFC makes no ≥44px claim while the handle renders 12px inline
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `SFC contains a ≥44px claim: true (line 186-187). Measured thumb inline size: 12px.` Re-introducing any '≥44px' / '>=44px' assertion in the SFC while G5b is RED fails it. This is the pair G5b needs: the geometry is banked on the producer, but the false claim about it is ours and leaves today.

gates.gate: G6 · NO LINE — the population contributes zero retained dividing lines
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `computed dividing lines on /#/atmosphere: 1 section rule + 1 action-bar rule = 2 (want 0; /#/blob = 8)`. Asserts COMPUTED border width, not source, so a producer-emitted line (ConfiguratorLayer's `dividers` prop passed truthy) counts too. Honest severity carried with the gate: composited alpha-correctly over the well these rules measure 1.24:1 light and 1.29:1 dark — forbidden by the boundary inventory AND too weak to group, so this is a clean deletion, not a contrast repair. The arm that gains force is forced-colors, where the same rules compute rgb(0,0,0) and are the only surviving element in the pane.

gates.gate: G7 · RESERVED READOUT — the live value is tabular and reserves its widest legal representation
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `font-variant-numeric "normal" (want tabular-nums); min-inline-size "auto"; narrowest "3" 6.8px → widest "-0.0005" 47.4px = 40.6px swing (want ≤ 0.5px)`. Deriving precision from the value rather than the declared step fails it — that is `fmt()` at SFC:84-86 today, which renders three decimals for a step-0.1 domain. This is the ONE value channel the pane can own while B-1 is banked: with the fill unreachable, the readout IS the value read, so it must be exact and it must not reflow.

gates.gate: G8 · TYPE LENS — the config lens is typed: zero laundering casts, zero `as number`
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `(x as unknown) as Record<string, unknown> in demo/scenes/ = 4 (want 0); as number in the SFC = 1 (want 0)`. Scoped to source per L-9 (no node_modules, no dist, no test-results). Any consumer re-laundering its config, or any re-introduced `as number` over a readPath result, fails it. The structural gate (L-8): once the lens is typed, C-5, D-16, D-11's precision axis, D-15's dependency axis and D-9's rank field are unrepresentable-if-wrong rather than merely gated.

gates.gate: G9 · ANTI-VACUITY — a unit suite exercises the pane's behaviour
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `Files under test/ + demo/test/ naming ConfigSliderPane: 0 (want > 0)`. The four named green-keeping mutations are the inputs that must make the NEW suite fail: M1 `update()` → no-op (all 34 sliders read-only), M2 `resetDefaults()` → no-op, M3 `copyAsJson()` → no-op, M4 `fmt(v)` → `String(v)`. All four survive today against 19 vitest files and two colour-only e2e oracles. Lands FIRST in build order for the adverse-oracle reason recorded under STRUCTURE.

gates.gate: G10a · ONE RECIPE PER ROLE — a heading is not a row label, and it steps above the rows it groups
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `.config-section-title vs .aurora-row-label computed-identical on 6/6 properties {ff:"Fira Code", fs:16.4px, fw:400, tt:uppercase, ls:1.64px, color:rgb(112,89,66)}; section heading 16.4px vs row label 16.4px — no size step`. Two failing inputs: any consumer re-declaring font-family/size on a row or heading, and any heading whose rendered size is ≤ its rows' label size.

gates.gate: G10b · NO FORK — no consumer re-mints the section-title recipe
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `aurora-row-label occurrences in AuroraPane.vue: 5 (want 0)`. The source gate that stops G10a from being satisfied by a byte-copy under a different class name — the exact shape the defect has today (AuroraPane.vue:194-200 is byte-identical to SFC:237-243 in all five declarations, same order).

gates.gate: G11 · DOC TRUTH — the SFC documents only what it declares and renders
gates.whatWouldMakeItFail: RED TODAY: `header documents extraControls? that defineProps never declares: true; JSDoc :44 promises an empty state and the template has no v-else: true`. Extends to the third stale claim in the same cut: SFC:103-105 asserts 'The scroll region owns the fade mask' against a measured `mask-image: none` (the class at PaneHeader.vue:54-57 sets only `contain` and `scroll-timeline`). Any documentation asserting behaviour the render tree does not contain fails it.
