result.dissent:
FIVE DISSENTS, each byte-grounded, plus one recorded against myself.

(1) AGAINST BOTH CHALLENGER SEATS AND BOTH PRIOR JURORS, ON THE VALUE-READ CURE — the most consequential disagreement in this adjudication. C-3, D-3, D-14 and JUROR-3's J3-01 all prescribe "retire variant='spectrum' so the producer's .slider-range paints the value", and JUROR-3's G1 gates on it demo-side. I measured the proposition three independent ways and it is false at glass-ui 7.0.0: (a) flipping data-variant to the real default "standard" (Slider.vue `variant:{default:"standard"}`) leaves rangeBg `oklab(0 0 0 / 0)` — still transparent — and collapses the thumb to width 0, because the thumb's width/opacity rule is `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb` ONLY; (b) `.glass-slider:not([data-variant=spectrum]) .slider-range` painting rules in dist/glass-ui.css = 0; (c) an injected consumer rule `.config-console .slider-range{background:oklch(0.55 0.19 25)!important}` STILL computes transparent, and feeding the documented `--slider-range-bg` moves `--liquid-fill-tint` to the new value while background-color does not move. The fill is unreachable from the demo at any specificity. JUROR-2 reached the same refutation independently and proposed the cascade-layer mechanism (`.glass-liquid-fill` is layered in dist/styles/glass/liquid-fill.css while the SFC-scoped `.slider-range[data-v-4f4cab01]` rules in glass-ui.css are unlayered); I verified that file exists and that glass-ui.css contains zero occurrences of `glass-liquid-fill`, and I adopt the mechanism as a HYPOTHESIS while the observation stands on its own. Consequence: a wave that gates the paint demo-side CANNOT CLOSE (L-1), and worse, retiring the variant today would strictly worsen the pane — the last remaining value cue, the thumb, disappears.

(2) AGAINST D-1's CAUSATION, AND AGAINST JUROR-3 UPHOLDING IT AS STATED. D-1 blames SFC:202 for the vanished forced-colors focus indicator and offers "grep -rn forced-colors demo/scenes/ returns zero hits" as evidence that no policy exists. Both are wrong, and the second is an L-9 scope error that hides a live, demo-owned, broken cure: demo/styles/foundation.css:678 ships a full two-tier WHCM policy and :702-720 binds `:where(… [role="slider"] …):focus-visible{outline:2px solid Highlight}`. I proved the rule is alive with a CONTROL inside the very same forced-colors run — the action-bar button one DOM level away gets `outline-style: solid, 2px` while the thumb gets "none". It is defeated only by specificity: `:where()` contributes 0, so the demo rule is (0,1,0) against the producer's (0,4,0) `outline:none`. This converts a BLOCKER attributed to a glass-owned material into a demo-owned one-line cascade fix that can land today, and it is the single most valuable thing this seat found. Neither challenger nor either prior juror located it. The same block's tier-1 roster line at :693 puts `forced-color-adjust:none` on a range whose background I measured as `rgba(0,0,0,0)` — a second dead demo declaration, also unnoticed.

(3) AGAINST BOTH CHALLENGERS AND JUROR-3 ON WCAG 2.5.8. C-8, D-5 and J3-12 all assert the 12px thumb is "half the WCAG 2.5.8 inline minimum" and book an SC violation. Measured row pitch is 67px with exactly one target per row, so 2.5.8's undersized-target SPACING EXCEPTION is satisfied and the SC is MET. The geometry is still wrong against the house floor (PROPORTION-AUDIT law 7) and the SFC's ≥44px claim is still false — both of which I gate — but booking a false SC violation is precisely the class of error L-9 exists to prevent, and it would have entered the registry unchallenged from three separate seats.

(4) AGAINST D-10's UNHANDLED-REJECTION ARM, IN FAVOUR OF C-4. D-10 asserts that `@click="copyAsJson"` on an async function makes a writeClipboard rejection an unhandled promise rejection. I installed an `unhandledrejection` listener and forced `writeText` to reject on the real button: zero events. glass-ui's `writeClipboard` catches internally and returns `{ok:false, reason}` — exactly as C-4 states. Two challenger seats contradict each other on a producer contract; C-4 is right, and D-10's cited `void writeClipboard(...)` idiom at three other call sites is a style convention, not a cure. The "zero result state" half of D-10 survives fully.

(5) AGAINST C-9 AND THE STANDING C10 A4 BOOK. Four accusations converge on "adopt `useConfiguratorState<T>`". I read the signature before believing it: it REQUIRES `presets: readonly ConfiguratorPreset<T>[]`, and `resetCurrent()` restores the ACTIVE PRESET's baseline. Adopting it does not give this pane "reset to these defaults" — it changes the pane's model to a preset model. The book stays OPEN and re-scoped; the wave's cure is smaller and cannot lie about its domain: reset exactly the SliderDef key paths the pane owns.

AGAINST MYSELF, RECORDED IN FULL (L-9). My first contrast pass reported the section divider at 5.22:1 light / 1.19:1 dark — the challenger's 1.08/5.03 inverted, and wrong for the identical reason: a 1×1-canvas helper that fills `#000` and then fills the sample returns the colour PRE-MULTIPLIED OVER BLACK for any alpha<1, fabricating a luminance. Re-solving α from two grounds gives 1.24:1 light and 1.29:1 dark — no scheme asymmetry exists in either direction. I caught this before reading any prior seat's return; JUROR-3 caught the same artifact in its own first pass independently. That convergence is the strongest evidence in the corpus that this is a HARNESS defect with reach far beyond this component: every ledger number produced by a fill-black-then-fill helper against an alpha<1 colour is unsound and should be swept.

NO DISSENT on C-1's mechanism, on the 6/6 type-recipe identity, or on the vacuous-gate finding: on those three, seats that could not see each other converged from different premises onto the same bytes, and I reproduced each independently. Per L-14's corollary I note explicitly that my agreement with two prior jury seats on several rows is NOT mutual corroboration — I derived every number in this return from my own probes before reading theirs, and wherever we agree I have named the measurement of mine that produced the agreement.
result.addendumClause:
### ADD-CSP · The configurator population (worker-O)

**CSP-O1 · A cure is admissible only if its own cure path is reachable from where it is booked.** A defect whose remedy lives in another party's tree is a BANK with a runnable re-trigger and a relay, never a gate in a wave that cannot turn it green. Before a wave prescribes "consume the producer's X", it MEASURES X in the installed dist and on the live page — attribute flip, token feed, and a consumer `!important` override, in that order. A prescribed cure that three such experiments refute is refuted, however many independent seats converged on it. (Derived from: four seats prescribing a `.slider-range` paint that is unreachable from the demo at glass-ui 7.0.0 at any specificity.)

**CSP-O2 · Two channels, and the second must survive forced colours — proven in CHROMIUM, with a same-register CONTROL.** Control extent, fill, selection and focus each carry at least two independent channels. `background` alone is one; `box-shadow` under `outline-style: none` is one and it is the wrong one — **focus uses `outline`**. Every forced-colors assertion asserts `matchMedia("(forced-colors: active)").matches === true` FIRST and FAILS when false: WebKit ignores the emulation, so a WebKit forced-colors frame is void evidence, not a green one. And every forced-colors gate carries a CONTROL element in the same run — a sibling the policy is expected to reach. Without the control, a *defeated* rule is indistinguishable from an *absent* one, and the cure gets booked against the wrong owner.

**CSP-O3 · A `:where()` policy is a suggestion, not a policy.** A cross-cutting accessibility or modality rule written at specificity 0 is defeated by any component's own rule and will silently not apply. Such a rule declares, next to itself, the highest specificity it must beat and the control element that proves it lands. A policy nobody can observe applying is a dead declaration with a live comment.

**CSP-O4 · Composite honestly or do not quote a ratio.** A contrast number for a colour with alpha < 1 is computed by recovering α (two grounds, or a parser) and compositing over the ACTUAL ground. A helper that fills `#000` and then fills the sample reports the colour pre-multiplied over black and fabricates a luminance — and because the artifact is symmetric it can produce a finding OR its exact inverse. Any ratio whose measurement command is not re-runnable, or whose helper is not stated, is not evidence. **Ratios already in the registry produced this way are re-measured or struck.**

**CSP-O5 · Name the floor you are asserting.** A geometry or contrast gate names the authority it enforces — WCAG SC, house law, or producer token — and never borrows an SC's authority for a house floor. An undersized target that satisfies 2.5.8's spacing exception is a house-floor row, not an SC violation. The honest form keeps the gate AND drops the false claim: they are different obligations with different owners.

**CSP-O6 · Reset restores a declared domain; a whole-object merge may not stand in for one.** Reset names the key paths the control surface owns, announces its result in a durable status region, and is paired with a compare affordance. Reset semantics decided by nesting depth — preserving state at depth 1 because it is absent from defaults, destroying it at depth 2 because its parent is present — is a defect even when both consumers' prose declares the intent correctly, because the prose is not the mechanism.

**CSP-O7 · Precision, unit and disclosure derive from the DECLARED domain, never from the current value.** A control schema declares step, unit, precision, disclosure rank and dependency. Live numbers use tabular figures and reserve their widest legal representation. A pane generic over "any object addressed by any dot-path string" can express none of these, so each becomes a defect its own type signature forbids curing — which is why the schema, not the stylesheet, is where this class of row is closed.

**CSP-O8 · An oracle that must be broken to fix the defect is a LOCK, and it is re-aimed in the same cut as the cure.** Before a wave changes a surface, it enumerates the gates asserting that surface and states, for each, whether the cure turns it RED. A gate born green against a defect's own remedy is retired and re-aimed, never preserved — preserving it is how the previous cure produced the defect being adjudicated now.

**CSP-O9 · A retired variant takes its shims with it.** Before a consumer stops declaring a producer variant, every rule keyed to that variant — including banked, owner-ruled restatements in the consumer's own stylesheet — is enumerated and dispositioned in the same cut. A shim whose selector silently stops matching is a bank that rotted without anyone deciding it.
